# webauthn — WebAuthn and passkeys

[All groups](README.md)

## webauthn decode

Decode and check WebAuthn artifacts from a registration or authentication: clientDataJSON (type, challenge, origin), authenticator data (RP ID hash, UP/UV/BE/BS flags, counter, AAGUID, credential ID and COSE public key as JWK/PEM, extensions), the attestation object (packed and fido-u2f signatures verified; none and others decoded), and assertion signatures against the registered key. Accepts a whole PublicKeyCredential JSON.

MCP tool: `webauthn_decode`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--credential` | string | A PublicKeyCredential as JSON (response.clientDataJSON, attestationObject or authenticatorData/signature, base64url). CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--client-data-json` | string | clientDataJSON, base64url or raw JSON. |
| `--attestation-object` | string | attestationObject, base64url (registration). |
| `--authenticator-data` | string | authenticatorData, base64url (authentication). |
| `--signature` | string | Assertion signature, base64url. |
| `--public-key` | string | Credential public key for assertions: COSE (base64url), JWK or PEM (CLI: @file). CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--alg` | string | Signature algorithm when public_key is a JWK or PEM (ES256, RS256, PS256, EdDSA). |
| `--expected-challenge` | string | Challenge the RP issued (base64url). |
| `--expected-origin` | string | Origin the ceremony must come from, e.g. https://example.com. |
| `--rp-id` | string | RP ID whose SHA-256 must be the rpIdHash. |
| `--require-uv` | bool | Fail when user verification was not performed. |
| `--prior-sign-count` | int | Last stored signature counter, to detect cloned authenticators. |
| `--metadata` | bool | Check the authenticator against the FIDO Metadata Service: model, certification, security status, attestation chain to the model's root (downloads and caches the MDS3 BLOB). |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## webauthn register

Register a passkey with a relying party: fetches (or takes) the creation options and checks them (challenge, user handle, algorithms, RP ID against the origin), makes the credential, submits it and reports whether the server accepts it. The authenticator is a software one (ES256, EdDSA or RS256; none, packed self attestation, packed with an attestation certificate chain, or fido-u2f) or, with authenticator=usb, a real security key over CTAP2 or U2F, whose attestation is verified locally (the person must touch the key: tell them first). Returns the credential for webauthn.login. tamper sends a deliberately broken response to test that the server rejects it.

MCP tool: `webauthn_register`. **Changes data at the remote system.**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string | Base URL of a FIDO2 conformance-style server API (/attestation/options, /attestation/result, /assertion/options, /assertion/result). |
| `--options-url` | string | Instead of server: URL that returns the options (POSTed options_body). |
| `--options-body` | json | JSON body for options_url (merged into the default body with server). |
| `--result-url` | string | Instead of server: URL that verifies the credential response. |
| `--page-url` | string | With options_url: page to load first for session cookies, as a browser would (default the site's root; none to skip). |
| `--result-field` | string | Nest the credential response under this key when posting to result_url. |
| `--result-extra` | json | Extra fields for the result body (e.g. {"username":"alice"}). |
| `--options` | string | Options JSON to answer instead of fetching them (offline when no result URL). CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--origin` | string | Origin the browser would report (default: the server's). |
| `--username` | string | Account name sent with server. Default `idpdbg-test`. |
| `--user-verified` | bool | Software authenticator: set the UV flag (a simulated PIN or biometric). Default `true`. |
| `--device` | string | Security key: index or path from fido.devices (default: the only one connected). |
| `--ctap` | string | Security key protocol: auto does what a browser does (CTAP2, or U2F when the key would need a PIN that is not available). Default `auto`. One of `auto`, `ctap2`, `u2f`. |
| `--pin` | string | Security key PIN, for user verification as a browser would ask for it (prefer env IDPDBG_PIN or a profile; from a terminal idpdbg asks). Never retried: a wrong PIN costs one of the key's attempts. Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_PIN`, redacted in traces. |
| `--authenticator` | string | software, or usb for a connected security key. Default `software`. One of `software`, `usb`. |
| `--resident-key` | bool | Security key: make a discoverable credential (stored on the key, using one of its slots). |
| `--metadata` | bool | Security key: check the key's attestation against the FIDO Metadata Service (model, certification, security status, chain to the model's root). |
| `--alg` | int | Software authenticator: COSE algorithm (-7 ES256, -8 EdDSA, -257 RS256); default the server's first supported. |
| `--attestation-format` | string | Software authenticator: attestation statement format: none, packed self attestation, packed with an attestation certificate (x5c), or fido-u2f (ES256 only). Default `none`. One of `none`, `packed`, `packed-x5c`, `fido-u2f`. |
| `--attestation-ca` | string | With packed-x5c or fido-u2f: certificate and private key (PEM) of the CA that issues the attestation certificate, one the relying party trusts; default a throwaway CA, whose root the result shows. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). Over MCP it must be passed in the call, never taken from a profile or the environment. |
| `--backup-eligible` | bool | Mark the credential as a synced passkey (BE and BS flags). |
| `--tamper` | string | Send a broken response; the check passes if the server rejects it. One of `wrong_origin`, `wrong_rp_id_hash`, `wrong_challenge`, `wrong_type`, `no_user_present`, `bad_attestation_signature`, `broken_attestation_chain`, `bad_attestation_certificate`. |
| `--out` | string | Also write the credential to this file (CLI only). |

## webauthn login

Sign in to a relying party with a credential from webauthn.register: fetches (or takes) the request options and checks them (challenge, RP ID, allowCredentials, user verification), signs an assertion with the next signature counter, submits it and reports whether the server accepts it. A credential made on a security key is used on that key (touch needed: tell the person first) and its signature checked locally. Returns the credential with its updated counter. tamper tests that the server rejects a wrong origin, RP ID, challenge or type, missing user presence or verification, a bad signature or a counter that did not increase.

MCP tool: `webauthn_login`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string | Base URL of a FIDO2 conformance-style server API (/attestation/options, /attestation/result, /assertion/options, /assertion/result). |
| `--options-url` | string | Instead of server: URL that returns the options (POSTed options_body). |
| `--options-body` | json | JSON body for options_url (merged into the default body with server). |
| `--result-url` | string | Instead of server: URL that verifies the credential response. |
| `--page-url` | string | With options_url: page to load first for session cookies, as a browser would (default the site's root; none to skip). |
| `--result-field` | string | Nest the credential response under this key when posting to result_url. |
| `--result-extra` | json | Extra fields for the result body (e.g. {"username":"alice"}). |
| `--options` | string | Options JSON to answer instead of fetching them (offline when no result URL). CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--origin` | string | Origin the browser would report (default: the server's). |
| `--username` | string | Account name sent with server. Default `idpdbg-test`. |
| `--user-verified` | bool | Software authenticator: set the UV flag (a simulated PIN or biometric). Default `true`. |
| `--device` | string | Security key: index or path from fido.devices (default: the only one connected). |
| `--ctap` | string | Security key protocol: auto does what a browser does (CTAP2, or U2F when the key would need a PIN that is not available). Default `auto`. One of `auto`, `ctap2`, `u2f`. |
| `--pin` | string | Security key PIN, for user verification as a browser would ask for it (prefer env IDPDBG_PIN or a profile; from a terminal idpdbg asks). Never retried: a wrong PIN costs one of the key's attempts. Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_PIN`, redacted in traces. |
| `--credential` | string | The credential from webauthn.register (idpdbg-webauthn:...) Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_CREDENTIAL`, redacted in traces. CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). Over MCP it must be passed in the call, never taken from a profile or the environment. |
| `--passkey` | bool | Instead of credential: a passkey sign-in with a security key, which finds the account itself (touch needed; tell the person first). |
| `--account` | string | Passkey sign-in with several accounts on the key: which one (user name, display name, user handle, or number); from a terminal idpdbg asks. |
| `--tamper` | string | Send a broken assertion; the check passes if the server rejects it. One of `wrong_origin`, `wrong_rp_id_hash`, `wrong_challenge`, `wrong_type`, `no_user_present`, `bad_signature`, `counter_not_increased`, `no_user_verified`. |
